name: Sliding Window
description: The sliding window pattern is used when you need to find some subarray or substring satisfying certain constraints, such as a maximum or minimum length. Instead of recomputing from scratch, you maintain a window defined by two pointers and slide it across the input, adding and removing elements at the edges.
how_to_identify: Look for 'subarray' or 'substring' that meets a condition, or fixed/maximum/minimum length over a contiguous range.
use_cases: Longest substring with at most K distinct characters
Maximum sum of a subarray of size K
Minimum window containing all characters of a target string
template: Expand right pointer; while window is invalid, shrink from the left; update the answer after adjusting the window.
time_complexity: O(N) — each element enters and leaves the window at most once
space_complexity: O(1) or O(alphabet) depending on what you track
common_mistakes: Confusing fixed-size windows with variable-size (shrinkable) windows.
Forgetting to update the answer at the correct point in the loop.
